# bugs #3337: sdcdb ends with a segmentation fault at break main for a z80 program

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3337/
- Category: [Already fixed in trunk](../../fixed-upstream.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r14664, the fix for bug #3529. Close bug #3270 with it, which shows this crash for mcs51.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

On r17176 sdcdb sets the breakpoint. A z80 program in the shape of the ticket's was compiled with
`-mz80 --code-loc 0x100 --no-std-crt0 --debug`. In `sdcdb -mz80`, the command `break main` printed
`Breakpoint 1 at 0x10d: file hello.c, line 22.`, and 0x10d is the address of `main` in the `.cdb`
file. For the program of bug #3270, compiled with `-mmcs51 --debug`, `break main` also set a
breakpoint at the address of `main`. Only the `break` command was checked. Whether execution stops
at the breakpoint was not examined.

## Fixed by

[r14664](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/14664/), the fix for bug #3529. Since r10450 the
compiler writes the scope level of a symbol in two parts, so the function record is
`F:G$main$0_0$0`, and the linker record of the function is `L:G$main$0$0`. Before r14664 sdcdb did
not match the two names, and the function kept the start and end addresses 0. `functionPoints` in
`debugger/mcs51/sdcdb.c` skips functions with these addresses and leaves their module pointer null.
`commonSetUserBp` passed that pointer to `setBPatModLine`, which is the top frame of the backtrace
in the ticket. r14664 adds `parseLevel` and `allocRName` to `debugger/mcs51/symtab.c`. They read
the two-part level and make the two names equal. The code that reads `.cdb` files is the same for
every port.

[r13800](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13800/) had added a check for a null module to
`setBPatModLine`.

## Related

Bug #3270 shows the same backtrace for an mcs51 program and is open. Its program is the second
one in the test above.
